text.p: Following are the top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Singapore will have a special entertainment hub, to be located in Selegie/Bugis area.
- Hardcore heroin, opium and morphine addicts are in for longer sentences if they are caught with drugs after being released, Home Affairs Minister Wong Kan Seng says.
- Seven-year-old Sunny Lam Pui impresses Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew with calligraphy when Lee visits Singapore International School in Hongkong.
- Parliament will sit on July 11 when members' questions will be answered orally by ministers, two bills read, and budget unveiled.
- Forum shopping mall on Orchard Road understood to have been offered to former real estate banker Simon Cheong for about Singapore S$380 million, say sources.
- Stock Exchange of Singapore may ease rules it introduced recently to tighten internal controls at listed companies.
- Nanyang Technological University economists lower their economic growth forecast for current year to 6.5 percent from 7.2 percent predicted in January.
- Confidence is palpable these days around Exchange Square, home to booming Hong Kong stock market, as last major bastion of British colonialism prepares for return to China.
- National Westminister Bank, Britain's biggest, says junior trader from investment banking arm had for two years covered up losses of 90 million sterling from high-risk options deals.
- Koh brothers subsidiary G&W Group says it has received in-principle approval for listing on mainboard of Stock Exchange of Singapore.
- An individual, Tan Seng Chai, revealed as buyer of First Capital Corp's entire 13.14 percent stake in Sesdaq-listed retailer Heshe Holdings.
- Transport group Tibs Holdings proposes one-for-one rights issue at 80 cents apiece to raise more than S$35 million to fund expanding China business.
- Banks holding Van der Horst shares pledged as collateral appear to have dumped much more of the stock than indicated by company managing director Michael Oxborrow.
- Singapore Technologies Industrial Corp investing S$8 million in second hotel project in China.
- Shares in Stamford Tyres resume trading and by close recover most of losses taken on news of last week's fire in company's Jurong warehouse.
